name: Graham
who: Retired electrician. Lives with his wife. Brother had a heart attack at 70.
opening: "Just my blood pressure script, doc."

actions.label: Side effects?
actions.text: No problems with the tablets. Takes them every morning.

actions.label: Smoking
actions.text: Ex-smoker. Quit 10 years ago after 30 years.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Thinks his blood pressure is "sorted". Quietly worried about his brother's heart attack. Expects a script and the car park.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.doorknob: "Oh, and by the way, I get a bit tight in the chest walking up the hill to the shops. Goes away when I stop."
actions.why: "Anything else?" was where the angina was hiding.

actions.label: Chest tightness: tell me more
actions.text: Central tightness on exertion for about 6 weeks. Eases within a few minutes of resting. Never at rest. None today.
actions.why: Characterising exertional chest pain is the whole consult once it's mentioned.

actions.label: Blood pressure
actions.text: 142/86. Pulse 78, regular.

actions.label: Heart, lungs, ankles
actions.text: Normal heart sounds, clear chest, no ankle swelling.

actions.label: ECG
actions.text: Sinus rhythm, no acute changes. A normal resting ECG doesn't rule out angina.
actions.why: New exertional chest pain earns an ECG today.

actions.label: Order lipids, HbA1c, kidney check
actions.text: Ordered: lipids, HbA1c, eGFR and urine albumin-creatinine ratio.

options: Short-acting GTN spray, with clear instructions
Prompt cardiology assessment for further testing
Lipids, HbA1c and kidney check, and a CVD risk review
Explain the plan and check he's understood (teach-back)
Reassure: probably just unfit. See you in 12 months
Call 000 if chest pain comes on at rest, is severe, is getting worse, or isn't fully gone within 10 minutes
Mention it at your next review if it's still there
Take two paracetamol and lie down
Drive yourself to ED if it gets bad

extras.label: Also bill a GP chronic condition management plan (965) today
extras.why: GPCCMP items can't be co-claimed with a general attendance on the same day. Book the plan as its own visit.

src.t: MBS Online: GP chronic condition management plans

extras.label: Mark the HbA1c request 'established diabetes' so it's rebated
extras.why: He doesn't have diabetes. 66551 is for monitoring established diabetes; a diagnostic HbA1c in an asymptomatic high-risk patient is 66841, once in 12 months.

extras.label: Item 11714: 12-lead ECG, trace plus your clinical note (indication and interpretation)
extras.why: You did the ECG and read it to decide what happens next. Since 1 March 2026 that's 11714 for a GP, on top of the consult. Keep the ECG minutes out of the consult tier.
extras.whyNo: No ECG was done, so there's no ECG to bill.

src.t: MBS Online: ECG items 11707 and 11714 amended (1 March 2026)

extras.label: Item 11707 for the same ECG
extras.why: 11707 is a trace sent to a specialist or consultant physician for a formal report. You interpreted this one yourself: that's 11714.

src.t: MBS Online: ECG items 11707 and 11714 amended (1 March 2026)

pearl: The "just a script" consult is where angina likes to hide. Leave room for "anything else?", and if the answer is chest pain on exertion, the plan isn't "see you next year".

name: Graham
criticalWhy: Chest pain at rest in the waiting room. Every minute in the queue is heart muscle.
who: Back again. You saw him for a repeat script.
opening: "It's happening walking to the letterbox now. Had a bad one this morning just sitting down."

actions.label: How has the pain changed?
actions.text: Now with minimal effort, and twice at rest. This morning's lasted about 15 minutes.
actions.why: Pain at rest or on minimal effort is the change that makes this unstable.

actions.label: Any pain right now?
actions.text: Mild tightness now. Started about 20 minutes ago in the waiting room.
actions.why: Ongoing pain right now changes everything about the next ten minutes.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Scared it's a heart attack, like his brother. Hoping for "a stronger pill".

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "Isn't that enough?" Fair.

actions.label: Obs: BP, pulse, sats
actions.text: BP 150/90, HR 92, sats 96% on air. Pale and clammy.
actions.why: Obs tell you how sick he is right now and whether GTN is safe.

actions.label: 12-lead ECG
actions.text: ST depression in the lateral leads.
actions.why: The ECG is quick and changes the urgency, but it shouldn't delay calling the ambulance.

actions.label: Send a troponin to the lab
actions.text: Result in hours. He needs a hospital, not a courier.
actions.why: A community troponin delays transfer and doesn't change what he needs.

options: Aspirin 300 mg, chewed or dissolved (unless contraindicated)
GTN spray while waiting, watching his blood pressure
Routine oxygen even though his sats are 96%
Send him home with a stronger tablet
Book an outpatient stress test next month
Stay with him, keep him monitored and send a summary with the ambulance
Let him wait in the car park for the ambulance
He can drive himself to hospital
Come back if it happens again

pearl: Angina that's new, worse or happening at rest is an acute coronary syndrome until proven otherwise. Aspirin, ECG, ambulance, in whichever order gets them all done fastest.

extras.label: Item 11714: 12-lead ECG, trace plus your clinical note (indication and interpretation)
extras.why: You did the ECG and read it to decide what happens next. Since 1 March 2026 that's 11714 for a GP, on top of the consult. Keep the ECG minutes out of the consult tier.
extras.whyNo: No ECG was done, so there's no ECG to bill.

src.t: MBS Online: ECG items 11707 and 11714 amended (1 March 2026)

extras.label: Item 11707 for the same ECG
extras.why: 11707 is a trace sent to a specialist or consultant physician for a formal report. You interpreted this one yourself: that's 11714.

src.t: MBS Online: ECG items 11707 and 11714 amended (1 March 2026)

name: Maya
criticalWhy: A floppy, feverish toddler is time-critical. Seeing her last means she waited longest.
who: Here with her dad, Emeka. Usually a chatterbox.
opening: "She's been hot since last night. Now she just wants to lie on me."

actions.label: Fever story
actions.text: Fever since last night. Vomited twice. Refusing drinks; only one wet nappy today.

actions.label: Immunisations
actions.text: Up to date for her age.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: "She's never been like this." He wants her checked properly, and he's right to.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.doorknob: "She screamed when I touched her legs this morning. She never does that."
actions.why: Leg pain is an early warning sign of meningococcal sepsis in children.

actions.label: Obs: temp, heart rate, cap refill
actions.text: Temp 39.4°C, HR 170, capillary refill 4 seconds. Cold hands and feet.
actions.why: Cold peripheries and slow cap refill in a febrile child are early sepsis signs.

actions.label: Check her skin all over
actions.text: Several purple spots on her legs that don't fade when you press a glass on them.
actions.why: A non-blanching rash with fever is meningococcal disease until proven otherwise.

actions.label: Neck and alertness
actions.text: Drowsy and irritable when handled. Neck hard to assess.

actions.label: Urine dipstick
actions.text: Three minutes of coaxing, no sample. The clock didn't wait.
actions.why: A urine sample was never going to change the plan for this child.

options: Parenteral antibiotics (benzylpenicillin or ceftriaxone) now, as long as it doesn't delay transfer
Phone the receiving hospital and hand over
Explain to her dad what's happening and why
Stay with them until the ambulance arrives
Back to the waiting room until the ambulance comes
Dad can drive her to ED if traffic's OK
Come back tomorrow if she's no better

pearl: In a febrile child: leg pain, cold hands and feet and pale or mottled skin can come before the rash. Once there's a non-blanching rash, antibiotics and an ambulance shouldn't wait for anything.

name: Priya
who: Accountant. Two kids under five. Vegetarian.
opening: "I'm just exhausted. I figured it's work."

actions.label: Mood and sleep
actions.text: Mood fine, still enjoys things. Sleeps 7 hours. No snoring.

actions.label: Diet
actions.text: Vegetarian, eats a varied diet.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Wonders about her thyroid (her mum has hypothyroidism). Expects blood tests.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.doorknob: "Also... my periods have got really heavy. I'm flooding through pads overnight."
actions.why: Heavy periods were the cause, and she only mentioned them because you asked.

actions.label: Periods: tell me more
actions.text: Heavy for 7 days with clots, changing pads every 1 to 2 hours on heavy days. Regular cycle. No bleeding between periods or after sex.
actions.why: A bleeding history shapes both the diagnosis and whether she needs imaging.

actions.label: Obs and colour
actions.text: Pale. HR 96, BP 112/70.

actions.label: Pelvic examination (with consent)
actions.text: With consent: no masses, uterus feels normal size.

actions.label: Full blood count and ferritin
actions.text: Hb 98 g/L (low). Ferritin 6 µg/L (typical range for women roughly 30 to 300).
actions.why: The standard says to check FBC and ferritin routinely in heavy menstrual bleeding.

actions.label: Thyroid function
actions.text: TSH normal.

actions.label: Pregnancy test
actions.text: Negative.

options: Iron deficiency anaemia from heavy menstrual bleeding
Discuss treatment for the heavy bleeding (e.g. hormonal IUD, tranexamic acid, NSAIDs)
Explain the plan and check she's understood (teach-back)
Pelvic ultrasound for everyone with heavy periods, regardless
More red meat and an early night
Come back sooner if you're breathless, faint, have chest pain, or the bleeding gets heavier
Stop the iron if your stools go dark

extras.label: Order TSH first (the lab adds free T4 only if TSH is abnormal)
extras.why: You don't bill this; the lab does. TSH is rebated as item 66716. Free T4/T3 (66719) is only rebated if the TSH is abnormal or a listed reason applies, so for a tired patient you request TSH and the lab does the rest.

extras.label: Also order vitamin D because she's tired
extras.why: Tiredness isn't a 66833 indication, so there's no rebate and Priya may get a bill.

extras.label: Item 35503 today, for the IUD discussion
extras.why: 35503 is the insertion itself. Talking through a hormonal IUD is part of today's consult; bill 35503 on the day it goes in.

pearl: "Tired all the time" in a menstruating woman: ask about periods, then check FBC and ferritin. The hormonal IUD is the most effective medical treatment for heavy bleeding when there's no significant pathology.

sources.t: Heavy Menstrual Bleeding Clinical Care Standard
Lifeblood: causes of iron deficiency anaemia

name: Tom
who: Apprentice carpenter. Started deadlifting last month.
opening: "Did deadlifts Saturday and my back's killing me. Can I get a scan and something strong?"

actions.label: Pain story
actions.text: Low back ache, worse bending. No pain down the legs.

actions.label: Bladder, bowel, saddle numbness
actions.text: No trouble passing urine, no bowel change, no numbness "down below".
actions.why: Cauda equina symptoms are the one thing you can't afford to skip in back pain.

actions.label: Fever, weight loss, cancer, injecting
actions.text: None.
actions.why: Screening for infection, malignancy and fracture is part of every back pain assessment.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Thinks he's "slipped a disc". Worried he'll lose his apprenticeship. Expects an MRI and oxycodone.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "Nah, that's it."

actions.label: Leg neuro exam
actions.text: Normal power, reflexes and sensation.
actions.why: A focused neuro exam is how you show yourself there's no nerve compromise.

actions.label: Back exam
actions.text: Tender muscles either side of the spine. Bending forward limited by pain.

actions.label: Lumbar X-ray
actions.text: Normal. Which you could have predicted.
actions.why: Imaging wasn't indicated: no red flags.

actions.label: MRI request
actions.text: Without alerting features, imaging isn't recommended, and incidental disc findings can frighten people.
actions.why: An MRI without red flags tends to find things that aren't the problem.

options: Stay active and keep doing usual activities, modified as needed
Simple pain relief to help him keep moving
Explain the plan and why no scan is needed (teach-back)
Review in 1 to 2 weeks if not improving
Come back the same day if you get bladder or bowel problems, numbness around the genitals or bottom, or leg weakness
Come back if it's not gone in 6 months
Take more tablets if it hurts more

pearl: Most acute back pain settles. Screen for red flags, examine, then sell activity. Bed rest is harmful and opioids are for carefully selected patients, lowest dose, shortest time.

sources.t: Low Back Pain Clinical Care Standard

name: June
criticalWhy: A head injury on an anticoagulant can bleed quietly. Seeing her last cost her hours.
who: Lives alone, gardens daily. Her daughter Eleni brought her in.
blurb: Fell last night. Daughter "a bit worried".
opening: "I'm fine, love. Eleni made me come."

actions.label: What happened?
actions.text: Tripped on a rug getting up to the toilet. Hit her head on the bedside table.
actions.why: A head strike changes this from a fall to a head injury.

actions.label: Medicines
actions.text: Apixaban for atrial fibrillation. Blood pressure tablet.
actions.why: Anticoagulation is the detail that makes this head injury urgent.

actions.label: Headache, vomiting, drowsiness
actions.text: Headache since. Vomited once this morning.
actions.why: Headache and vomiting after a head injury need asking about every time.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Worried she'll be "put in a home". Wants a quick check and to get back to her tomatoes.

actions.label: "Anything else?" (to Eleni too)
actions.doorknob: Eleni: "She's been asking me the same question over and over this morning."
actions.why: New repetitive questioning after a head injury is a worrying change.

actions.label: Obs
actions.text: BP 150/80, HR 88 irregular. Alert, but asks you the same thing twice.

actions.label: Head and neuro exam
actions.text: Bruise over the right temple. No focal weakness.

actions.label: Finger-prick glucose
actions.text: 6.1 mmol/L.

actions.label: Routine bloods
actions.text: Results tomorrow. Not much use today.
actions.why: Routine bloods don't answer the question that matters today: is she bleeding inside her head?

options: Head injury while on an anticoagulant: needs urgent CT
Same-day transfer to ED for a CT head scan
Explain the plan to June and Eleni, and check they've understood
Restart and carry on with apixaban as usual
Ice pack and home with Eleni
If she gets drowsier, more confused, vomits again or the headache worsens before she's seen, call 000

extras.label: Also bill a 75+ health assessment (701 to 707) today
extras.why: Today was an acute head injury, not a health assessment. You can only bill a health assessment you actually did; book one when she's well.

pearl: NICE suggests considering a CT head within 8 hours of injury for anyone on an anticoagulant, even with no other indication. Add vomiting and new repetitive questioning, and the decision makes itself.

name: Jayden
who: Aboriginal boy from a remote community. Here with his nan, Aunty Rose.
opening: Aunty Rose: "He's had a sore throat for two days and he's off his food."

actions.label: Symptoms
actions.text: Sore throat and fever. No cough.

actions.label: Rheumatic fever history
actions.text: His cousin has rheumatic heart disease. Jayden hasn't had rheumatic fever.
actions.why: Living in a high-risk setting, with family history, is what decides treatment.

actions.label: Skin sores
actions.text: A few healing school sores on his legs.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Aunty Rose asks if he'll need "the needle every month" like his cousin. Hopes he's back at school soon.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "No, that's it."

actions.label: Throat and neck
actions.text: Red tonsils, tender neck glands.

actions.label: Heart and joints
actions.text: No murmur. No joint swelling.

actions.label: Throat swab
actions.text: Sent. In a high-risk setting, treatment shouldn't wait for it.

options: Viral sore throat: no treatment needed
Sore throat in a child at high risk of acute rheumatic fever
Penicillin treatment now (first-line for sore throat in high-risk groups)
Treat the skin sores as well
Explain to Jayden and Aunty Rose, and answer the needle question honestly
Wait for the swab before deciding
Come back if he gets sore or swollen joints, breathlessness or chest pain, or isn't improving in a few days
Only come back if the throat's still sore in a month
Come back if he gets a cough

extras.label: Also bill a 715 health assessment today
extras.why: A 715 is a full health assessment with set components and a 9-month gap rule. A sore-throat consult isn't one, however good. Offer to book one.

pearl: Where rheumatic fever is common, a sore throat or skin sore is a prevention opportunity. Treat with penicillin, treat the skin, and make sure follow-up is easy.
cu: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health

name: Mei
who: Primary school teacher. Last period 2 years ago.
opening: "The night sweats are wrecking my sleep. My friend says HRT changed her life."

actions.label: Symptoms
actions.text: About 10 flushes a day. Wakes drenched most nights.

actions.label: Past history
actions.text: No personal history of breast cancer or blood clots. Non-smoker.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Worried hormones cause cancer. Hoping to leave with a script today.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.doorknob: "Oh, I've had a bit of spotting the last couple of months. Probably nothing?"
actions.why: Bleeding after menopause needs investigating before MHT starts.

actions.label: Spotting: tell me more
actions.text: Light spotting three times in two months. No pain.
actions.why: Postmenopausal bleeding is a red flag in its own right.

actions.label: Speculum exam (with consent)
actions.text: Cervix looks normal. No obvious source of bleeding.

options: Menopause symptoms plus postmenopausal bleeding that needs investigating
Investigate the bleeding first (transvaginal ultrasound, then gynaecology as needed)
When MHT is appropriate: combined oestrogen and progestogen, as she has a uterus
Explain the plan and check she's understood (teach-back)
Tell her spotting is normal after menopause
Let us know about any further bleeding, and come back for the ultrasound results

pearl: MHT is the most effective treatment for hot flushes, but any unexplained vaginal bleeding gets investigated before it's prescribed. With a uterus, oestrogen always comes with a progestogen.

name: Sam
who: Works in hospitality. Uses they/them. Plays club rugby.
opening: "I just need something to help me sleep."

actions.label: Sleep
actions.text: Awake until 3am most nights for two months.

actions.label: Mood and interest
actions.text: Low most days. Stopped going to training. Eating less.

actions.label: Ask directly about suicide
actions.text: "Sometimes I think everyone'd be better off without me." No plan. No previous attempts.
actions.why: Asking directly is safe, and people often won't volunteer it unless asked.

actions.label: Alcohol and drugs
actions.text: Drinking more on weekends.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Thinks it's "just stress". Worried about being judged. Hoped for sleeping tablets.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.doorknob: "My housemate moved out last month. It's pretty quiet at home now."

actions.label: Mental state
actions.text: Flat, quiet, good eye contact. No signs of injury.

actions.label: Depression questionnaire
actions.text: Scores in the severe range.

options: Make a safety plan together (warning signs, people and services to contact)
Book a review within days, not months
Crisis contacts: Lifeline 13 11 14, or 000 in an emergency
Explain the plan and check they've understood
Sleeping tablets and a review in 3 months
If the thoughts get stronger or you start making plans: call 000 or Lifeline (13 11 14), or go to ED
Come back if you're still not sleeping in 3 months
Try not to think about it
Have a drink to help you sleep

pearl: "Can't sleep" is a common ticket of entry for depression. Ask about suicide directly and kindly; it doesn't plant the idea, and it may be the only way you find out.

extras.label: Also bill a mental health treatment plan (2700) because you arranged therapy
extras.why: A plan (2700) needs at least 20 minutes on the plan itself and its required components, with its own time if you also bill a 23. Arranging therapy in a standard consult isn't a plan. Book a long appointment for it, soon.

src.t: RACGP: MBS mental health item changes for GPs

name: Sam
criticalWhy: Someone at immediate risk sat in the waiting room the longest.
who: Back again, with their friend Jess. You saw Sam about sleep.
opening: Jess: "Sam sent me a message last night that really scared me."

actions.label: Ask directly about suicide
actions.text: "I've been thinking about it a lot. I looked up ways last night."
actions.why: You can't judge risk without asking directly.

actions.label: Access to means
actions.text: Has been saving up tablets at home.
actions.why: Access to means is one of the most modifiable risks.

actions.label: Who's around?
actions.text: Jess can stay with Sam today.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Sam is ashamed and frightened. Jess wants to know Sam will be safe tonight.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "I didn't tell you everything last time."

actions.label: Mental state
actions.text: Tearful, hopeless. Says they can't keep themselves safe right now.
actions.why: Whether they can stay safe right now decides where they go next.

actions.label: Routine bloods
actions.text: Not the priority right now.
actions.why: Bloods can wait. Safety can't.

options: Depression with high, immediate suicide risk
Urgent same-day crisis assessment (acute mental health team or ED)
Sam isn't left alone: Jess stays until handover
Reduce access to means (the saved tablets)
Explain what happens next, to Sam and Jess
Home with a review in a fortnight
If at any point Sam can't stay safe before the assessment: call 000
Leave it to Sam to decide

pearl: When someone can't keep themselves safe, the plan is same-day crisis care, someone with them, and less access to means. Ask, act, and hand over warmly.

name: Abdi
who: Arrived in Australia 4 months ago as a refugee. Somali speaker. Just started work as a delivery driver.
opening: (In Somali, gesturing to a form) "Cough... and the form, for my job."

actions.label: Book a phone interpreter (TIS)
actions.text: A Somali interpreter joins. Now you can actually take a history.

actions.label: Cough details
actions.text: Cough for 6 weeks. Some blood-streaked sputum.
actions.why: A cough over three weeks, especially with blood, is a TB flag.

actions.label: Fevers, sweats, weight
actions.text: Night sweats. Lost about 6 kg.
actions.why: Night sweats and weight loss complete the TB picture.

actions.label: Who lives with you?
actions.text: His wife and three children.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Worried he'll lose his new job. Expects cough medicine and a signed form.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.doorknob: "My cousin had TB in the camp."
actions.why: A known TB contact raises the stakes considerably.

actions.label: Chest and temperature
actions.text: Crackles at the right upper chest. Temp 37.8°C.

actions.label: Chest X-ray and sputum for TB
actions.text: Requested: chest X-ray and sputum samples for TB testing.
actions.why: Chest X-ray and sputum are the first tests for suspected lung TB.

options: Chest X-ray and sputum tests for TB
Contact the local TB (chest) clinic urgently: assessment and treatment are free
Explain the plan through the interpreter and check understanding
Cough syrup and sign the fit-for-work form
Come back urgently if you cough more blood or get breathless
Come back if the cough lasts another 6 weeks

pearl: A cough of 3 weeks or more with sweats and weight loss in someone from a high-TB setting needs a chest X-ray and sputum. And a professional interpreter, not a mime.

name: Lachlan
who: Has Down syndrome. Lives in supported accommodation, works at a café. Here with his support worker, Kelly.
opening: Lachlan: "I'm tired. I want to go to work."

actions.label: Ask Lachlan himself
actions.text: Lachlan tells you he's "cold all the time" and his "tummy is stuck" (constipated).

actions.label: History from Kelly (with his OK)
actions.text: Slower at work over 6 months, gained 5 kg, dry skin. No change in routine or living situation.

actions.label: When was his thyroid last checked?
actions.text: No record of a TSH test in 3 years.
actions.why: People with Down syndrome have a much higher risk of hypothyroidism, rising with age.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Lachlan wants to keep his café job. Kelly is worried it's "early dementia".

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: Kelly: "He's been falling asleep on the bus home."

actions.label: Obs and examination
actions.text: HR 56. Weight up 5 kg. Dry skin. Slow-relaxing reflexes.

actions.label: TSH and free T4
actions.text: TSH 38 mIU/L (typical range about 0.4 to 4), free T4 low.
actions.why: A thyroid test is the cheapest test that rules a treatable cause in or out.

options: Start thyroid hormone replacement with a follow-up TSH
Explain to Lachlan in plain language, check he's understood, and include Kelly with his OK
Regular thyroid checks from now on
Refer to a memory clinic for dementia
Repeat the blood test in about 6 weeks, and come back sooner if he's getting worse
Only come back if he stops working

pearl: Don't let a disability explain away new symptoms (diagnostic overshadowing). Talk to the patient first, then the support worker, and check the thyroid.

sources.t: NICE indicator IND79: TSH testing in Down syndrome
Pathology Tests Explained: free T4 and TSH

name: Ron
who: Retired farmer. Fair skin, decades outdoors, hats optional until recently.
opening: "The wife says these scabby bits on my arms need looking at. Just freeze the lot, doc."

actions.label: Story of the spots
actions.text: Rough patches on both forearms for a year or two. They sting a bit in the sun.

actions.label: Any spot changing?
actions.text: One on the back of his left hand has grown over two months. It's sore to touch and bled once.
actions.why: Tender, fast-growing, bleeding: the features that suggest a keratosis has turned into a squamous cell carcinoma.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Thinks they're "just sunspots". Quietly worried after his brother's skin cancer operation. Expects you to freeze everything today.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "Nah, just the skin."

actions.label: Arms and hands, with dermoscopy
actions.text: Six rough, scaly pink patches on the forearms. On the back of the left hand: a 9 mm tender, raised, crusted nodule.
actions.why: You can't tell keratoses from cancers without looking properly.

actions.label: Lymph nodes (elbow and armpit)
actions.text: No enlarged nodes.
actions.why: With a suspected SCC, check the draining nodes.

actions.label: Biopsy the hand nodule (to pathology)
actions.text: With consent, under local anaesthetic, deep enough to assess invasion. Specimen sent for histology.
actions.why: When SCC can't be excluded, histology decides the plan.

actions.label: Cryotherapy to the 6 forearm keratoses
actions.text: One freeze-thaw cycle each. Warned about redness, blistering and pale marks.

actions.label: Freeze the hand nodule too
actions.text: Frozen. Along with the evidence.
actions.why: Avoid cryotherapy when the diagnosis is uncertain.

options: Solar keratoses only: freeze the lot
Solar keratoses, plus a hand lesion suspicious for squamous cell carcinoma
Biopsy the hand lesion and send it for histology
Treat the forearm keratoses (for example, cryotherapy)
Review with the histology result to plan definitive treatment
Explain the plan and check he's understood (teach-back)
Freeze the hand lesion and skip the biopsy
Come back sooner if the hand spot grows or bleeds, or you notice a lump in your elbow or armpit. We'll book you in for the result.
Pop some cream on it and see how it goes

extras.label: Item 30071: diagnostic skin biopsy, specimen sent for pathology
extras.why: A separate diagnostic biopsy sent for histology is its own item on top of a genuine consult. Don't count the biopsy minutes toward the time tier.

extras.label: Item 30192 for the cryotherapy to the 6 keratoses
extras.why: 30192 needs 10 or more premalignant lesions. Fewer than 10 solar keratoses treated ablatively are covered by the attendance item.

pearl: Freeze what you're sure of; biopsy what you're not. Billing-wise: fewer than 10 keratoses frozen sit inside the consult item, 30192 starts at 10, and a biopsy sent to pathology is its own item (30071).

sources.t: Medicine Today 2026: sun damage to keratinocyte cancer
Services Australia: skin lesion and biopsy billing

name: Zara
who: Barista. First pregnancy, she thinks.
opening: "My period's two weeks late and the test from the chemist was positive. What happens now?"

actions.label: Last period and cycle
actions.text: First day of last period about 6 weeks ago. Regular 28-day cycles.
actions.why: Dates the pregnancy and tells you what to expect on any scan.

actions.label: Pain or bleeding
actions.text: No pain, no bleeding.
actions.why: Pain or bleeding in early pregnancy means ectopic pregnancy must be thought about.

actions.label: How she feels about the pregnancy
actions.text: "Surprised. Happy, I think. My partner's thrilled."
actions.why: Asking, without assuming, lets her say if she's unsure and need options.

actions.label: Medicines, alcohol, smoking
actions.text: No regular medicines. Had a few drinks before she knew. Doesn't smoke.
actions.why: Reassure, then advise stopping alcohol now.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "Is it bad I haven't been taking any vitamins?"

actions.label: Urine pregnancy test in the room
actions.text: Positive.
actions.why: Confirms the pregnancy today, and you can bill it (73806).

options: Early pregnancy, about 6 weeks, no warning signs
Start folic acid and iodine supplements
Arrange first antenatal blood tests and a dating plan
Talk through her options and choices, without assuming
Explain warning signs and when to get help (teach-back)
Tell her it's too late, the vitamins won't help now
Book an urgent emergency department visit today
Go to the emergency department straight away for strong one-sided tummy pain, shoulder-tip pain, heavy bleeding or fainting
Come back if you're worried at the 20-week scan
Bleeding in early pregnancy is always normal
No need to come back until the baby's due

extras.label: Item 73806: urine pregnancy test done in the room
extras.why: A GP-performed urine pregnancy test is its own item, co-claimed with the consult. (This one you do bill: you did the test.)

src.t: CESPHN: Antenatal and pregnancy MBS items (Aug 2026), worked example

extras.whyNo: You didn't do the test in the room, so there's no 73806 to bill.

extras.label: Item 16500: antenatal attendance, once the pregnancy is confirmed and antenatal care starts
extras.why: The PHN worked example bills the initial suspected-pregnancy consult as 23, the in-room test as 73806, then 16500 for the antenatal care. Record the times for each part. Check MBS Online's antenatal notes before you rely on it.

src.t: CESPHN: Antenatal and pregnancy MBS items (Aug 2026), worked example

extras.label: Triple bulk billing incentive on the antenatal item
extras.why: Antenatal attendances get the single bulk billing incentive, not the triple.

src.t: CESPHN: Antenatal and pregnancy MBS items (Aug 2026), worked example

pearl: Early pregnancy visit: confirm, date it, start folic acid and iodine, ask how she feels about it without assuming, and give clear ectopic warning signs. In the room, the urine test is yours to bill.

sources.t: CESPHN: Antenatal and pregnancy MBS items (Aug 2026), worked example

name: Noor
who: Pharmacist. Two kids, done for now. Your practice bulk bills everyone.
opening: "I'm here for the Mirena. The pharmacist in me has read the product information twice."

actions.label: Last period and sex since
actions.text: Period started 4 days ago. No sex since. Using condoms until today.
actions.why: Insertion needs pregnancy reasonably excluded.

actions.label: STI risk and pelvic infection
actions.text: Long-term partner. No symptoms, no past pelvic infection.
actions.why: Current or recent pelvic infection must be treated and cleared before insertion.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Worried about the pain of insertion. Expects lighter periods. Wants it done today.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.doorknob: "Oh, am I due for my cervical screening? I think it's been over five years."
actions.why: "Anything else?" found an overdue screening test you can do in the same speculum exam.

actions.label: Speculum and bimanual exam (with consent)
actions.text: Healthy-looking cervix. Uterus anteverted, normal size, non-tender. No adnexal tenderness.
actions.why: Uterine position and size guide a safe insertion.

actions.label: Urine pregnancy test in the room
actions.text: Negative.
actions.why: Belt and braces before insertion.

actions.label: Take her cervical screening test
actions.text: Sample taken before insertion. Lab to bill the test.
actions.why: Overdue screening, speculum already in: do it now.

actions.label: Insert the hormonal IUD
actions.text: Inserted without difficulty. Strings trimmed. Batch and expiry recorded.
actions.why: The reason she came.

actions.label: Pelvic ultrasound before insertion
actions.text: Booked. She'll need another appointment.
actions.why: Not routinely needed before a straightforward insertion.

options: Suitable for hormonal IUD insertion today, and due for cervical screening
Not suitable: needs an ultrasound first
Insert the hormonal IUD with consent, and record batch and expiry
Take her cervical screening test today
Explain what to expect (cramping, irregular bleeding in the first months) and check understanding (teach-back)
Book a device check in a few weeks
Use backup contraception for 7 days, or skip it: insertion was in the first 5 days of her cycle
Insert it without discussing side effects to save time
Come back straight away for worsening pelvic pain, fever, unusual discharge, if you can't feel the strings, or think you might be pregnant
Some pain for a few months is normal, so ignore it
No need for follow-up unless it falls out
Take antibiotics if you get cramps

extras.label: Item 35503: IUD insertion
extras.why: The insertion is its own procedure item on top of the separate screening work.
extras.whyNo: You didn't insert the IUD, so there's no 35503.

extras.label: Item 35501: LARC loading (everything is bulk billed today)
extras.why: 35501 adds 40% of the LARC fee when the LARC service and its other items are bulk billed, in the same claim.
extras.whyNo: No IUD today, so no LARC item to load.

extras.label: Item 73806: urine pregnancy test done in the room
extras.why: You did the test: 73806, as in the sexual health guide's worked example (23 + 35503 + 73806).
extras.whyNo: No test was done in the room.

src.t: CERSH (Uni Melbourne): SRH MBS guide, Nov 2025 update

extras.label: Item 14206 for the device
extras.why: 14206 is hormone implantation by cannula (the implant), not an IUD.

extras.label: A consumables fee charged on top of the bulk-billed claim
extras.why: When you bulk bill, the benefit is full payment. No extra charges for any reason.

pearl: IUD day: exclude pregnancy, check for infection, consent properly, and ask "anything else?" while the speculum is handy. Billing: a separate screening test earns the 23, the insertion is 35503, the room test is 73806, and bulk billing earns the 35501 loading. No gap fees on a bulk-billed claim.

sources.t: CERSH (Uni Melbourne): SRH MBS guide, Nov 2025 update
RACGP: IUD and IUS checklist for GPs

name: Dean
who: Truck driver. Long shifts, servo dinners. Hasn't seen a GP in years.
opening: "Got a boil in my armpit that's killing me. Can you just lance it?"

actions.label: Story of the lump
actions.text: Started 4 days ago, getting bigger and more painful. Second one this year.
actions.why: Duration and recurrence shape the plan.

actions.label: Fever or feeling unwell
actions.text: No fevers or chills. Eating and drinking fine.
actions.why: Systemic illness or spreading infection changes whether antibiotics are needed.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Thinks it's "just a boil". Worried about missing shifts. Expects it lanced and antibiotics.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.doorknob: "While I'm here, the chemist said my blood pressure was 165 over 100. Is that bad?"
actions.why: "Anything else?" turned up a separate problem that needs its own plan.

actions.label: Blood pressure: tell me more
actions.text: Never treated. Smokes 10 a day. Dad had a stroke at 60.
actions.why: Untreated high readings and risk factors: this needs confirming, not ignoring.

actions.label: Examine the lump
actions.text: 3 cm fluctuant, tender swelling in the left armpit. Small rim of redness, no spreading cellulitis.
actions.why: Fluctuance means pus to drain; little surrounding redness means drainage alone may do.

actions.label: Blood pressure
actions.text: 158/98, and 156/96 on repeat.

actions.label: Incise and drain (local anaesthetic)
actions.text: Pus drained, cavity irrigated and packed, dressing on.
actions.why: Drainage is the main treatment for an abscess.

actions.label: Swab the pus
actions.text: Sent for culture, as this is his second abscess.

options: Skin abscess, plus raised blood pressure that needs confirming
Dressing review in 1 to 2 days (packing out)
Confirm his blood pressure with home or 24-hour ambulatory monitoring, then review
Explain the plan and check he's understood (teach-back)
Ignore the BP: it's just the pain
Come back the same day if the redness spreads, red streaks appear, you get fevers or it gets more painful. Chest pain, severe headache or weakness with high BP: call 000
Squeeze it again if it fills up
Finish the leftover antibiotics in your cupboard
Back in a month for the blood pressure

extras.label: Item 30219: incision and drainage of abscess
extras.why: Drainage of an abscess not needing hospital admission is 30219. The BP problem is separate, so the consult is legitimate too.
extras.whyNo: You didn't drain it, so there's no 30219.

extras.label: Item 30064 (subcutaneous foreign body removal)
extras.why: 30064 is for a foreign body needing incision and exploration. Pus isn't a foreign body.

extras.label: Item 30219 again at his dressing review
extras.why: 30219 excludes aftercare, so the dressing review is an attendance item, not another drainage.

src.t: Services Australia: aftercare or post-operative treatment

pearl: Drain the pus; antibiotics are for spreading infection or systemic illness. And always ask "anything else?": an untreated BP of 165/100 is a bigger long-term risk than the boil. Billing: 30219 excludes aftercare, so dressing reviews are attendances.

sources.t: Services Australia: aftercare or post-operative treatment
Frontiers in Microbiology 2016: GP management of staphylococcal skin abscesses in Australia

name: Helen
who: Retired teacher. Came alone.
opening: "The radiology place said you'd go through the scan with me."

actions.label: What she knows already
actions.text: "They were checking my weight loss. I've been expecting something."
actions.why: Start with what the patient knows before giving news.

actions.label: Warning shot
actions.text: "I'm afraid the scan has shown something serious." She nods and goes quiet.
actions.why: A warning shot gives a moment to prepare.

actions.label: Who's with her
actions.text: Her husband's at work. Her sister lives nearby.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: She's frightened of pain. Wants to know "how long" but isn't sure she wants the answer yet.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "Will I still be able to see my grandson's graduation in March?"

actions.label: Read the CT report
actions.text: Mass in the pancreatic head with liver lesions, likely metastases.

actions.label: Ask how much detail she wants
actions.text: "Just the main bits today please."
actions.why: People vary in how much they want at once. Ask.

actions.label: Explain the scan word for word
actions.text: You read out the radiology report. She looks lost.
actions.why: Reading out jargon isn't explaining. Chunk and check.

options: Likely advanced pancreatic cancer: needs urgent specialist work-up
Urgent referral to a hepatobiliary or oncology team, and call the specialist yourself
Share news in small chunks and check understanding
Offer to call her sister or husband to come in
Give a prognosis in months today
Book a follow-up within days and give her a direct number
Come back or call any time this week; book a review in a few days

extras.label: Bill a long consult (40+ minutes) item if you spent that time
extras.why: Time-based items reflect total time, including the conversation and arranging care.

pearl: Breaking bad news: set it up, find out what they know, ask how much they want, warn, give it in chunks, sit with the emotion, and make a plan with a next contact.

name: Darren
who: Tradie. Waited 50 minutes.
opening: "Fifty minutes! I've lost half a day's pay for this."

actions.label: Acknowledge and apologise for the wait
actions.text: "Fair enough. Sorry for the wait, that's frustrating." His shoulders drop a bit.
actions.why: Acknowledging emotion first defuses most anger.

actions.label: Explain the doctor was busy
actions.text: "Everyone's busy, mate." He gets louder.
actions.why: Defending yourself first escalates. Acknowledge, then move on.

actions.label: Reason for visit
actions.text: Right shoulder pain for 3 weeks. Worse lifting overhead.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Worried he'll lose work. Wants a scan and "a cortisone shot".

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "No. Just want to get back to work."

actions.label: Shoulder exam
actions.text: Painful arc. Strength OK. Pain on resisted abduction.
actions.why: Examination guides whether imaging is needed at all.

actions.label: Work duties
actions.text: Lifts plasterboard overhead most days.

actions.label: Order shoulder ultrasound today
actions.text: Ordered.
actions.why: Most rotator cuff tendinopathy doesn't need imaging at first. Try 6 weeks of rehab.

options: Explain the likely diagnosis and a 6-week physio and load plan
Come back if not improving in 6 weeks, or sooner if he loses strength or can't lift his arm
Only come back for a scan

extras.label: Bill a workers compensation claim to Medicare
extras.why: If it's a work injury claim, it's billed to the insurer, not Medicare. Here, it's not a claim yet: discuss whether it's work-related.

pearl: Anger is usually fear or frustration. Acknowledge it first, then the consult can start.

sources.t: RACGP Code of conduct and professionalism

name: Isla
who: Here with her dad, Josh.
opening: Josh: "She's two and only says about five words. Her cousin talks heaps."

actions.label: Developmental history
actions.text: Walked at 13 months. Few gestures. Doesn't point to show things.
actions.why: Missing pointing and social gestures matter more than word count.

actions.label: Hearing and ear infections
actions.text: Lots of ear infections last winter.
actions.why: Always check hearing in speech delay.

actions.label: Eye contact and play
actions.text: Lines up toys. Doesn't respond much to her name.
actions.why: Social communication differences suggest autism should be assessed.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Josh worries it's "something we did". Wants to know if it's autism.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "Her mum thinks I'm overreacting."

actions.label: Observe play and interaction
actions.text: Little shared attention. Engaged with a spinning top.

actions.label: Growth and head circumference
actions.text: On her centiles.

actions.label: Reassure: "some kids talk late"
actions.text: Josh looks relieved but unconvinced.
actions.why: "Wait and see" delays early help.

options: Possible autism and/or hearing loss: needs assessment
Refer for developmental assessment (paediatrician or child development service)
Speech pathology referral now, not after diagnosis
Tell Josh it's not his fault
Come back if she loses any skills, or for review in 4 to 6 weeks to check referrals are moving
Only if she gets an ear infection

extras.label: Bill a GP item for autism or developmental assessment as a referral to a paediatrician
extras.why: GPs refer; the specific diagnostic and treatment-plan items are for paediatricians and psychiatrists. A normal GP consult item applies.

pearl: Loss of skills at any age, or no pointing or babbling by 12 months, needs prompt assessment. Early help works best.

name: Kai
who: Here with his mum, Tash.
opening: Tash: "His arm's been swollen since yesterday. Not sure what happened."

actions.label: How it happened
actions.text: Unsure. Says he "might've rolled" on the change table.
actions.why: A vague or changing story in a non-mobile baby is a red flag.

actions.label: Can he roll yet?
actions.text: Not yet.
actions.why: Injury that doesn't match developmental stage raises concern.

actions.label: Who's at home
actions.text: Tash, her new partner, and Kai.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Tash is anxious and tearful. Wants it fixed quickly.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "I'm just so tired. He cries all night."

actions.label: Arm exam
actions.text: Swollen and tender upper arm.

actions.label: Full skin check
actions.text: Small bruises on his chest and behind his ear.
actions.why: Any bruise in a baby who can't move about on his own needs explaining.

actions.label: X-ray arm
actions.text: Spiral fracture of the humerus.

options: Send to the children's hospital ED today for assessment (skeletal survey, child protection team)
Make a mandatory report to child protection
Support Tash, be honest that you need to involve others
Sling and review in a week
Ask Tash's partner to come in and explain
Today's plan is hospital, not home. You'll follow up with Tash after
Come back if it swells more

extras.label: Bill a normal consult item
extras.why: Time and complexity apply. There's no special child protection item.

pearl: Bruises in babies who don't cruise rarely bruise. Unexplained injury in an infant needs hospital assessment and a report.

name: Ethan
who: Apprentice electrician. Booked for a "check-up".
opening: "Just need something to help me sleep."

actions.label: Mood
actions.text: "Flat. Not enjoying anything." Broke up with his partner a month ago.

actions.label: Ask directly about suicide
actions.text: "Yeah... I've thought about it. Last week I looked up ways."
actions.why: Asking directly doesn't put the idea there. It opens the door.

actions.label: Plans, means, protective factors
actions.text: Has a plan. Access to medicines at home. Loves his dog and his younger sister.
actions.why: Plan and access to means change the urgency and the safety plan.

actions.label: Alcohol and drugs
actions.text: Drinking more. 8 beers most nights.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Embarrassed. Doesn't want his boss to know.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "I don't want to end up in hospital."

actions.label: K10 questionnaire
actions.text: High (35).

actions.label: Prescribe sleeping tablets
actions.text: A month of temazepam.
actions.why: Sedatives give access to means and don't treat the cause.

options: Depression with suicidal thoughts and a plan
Collaborate on a written safety plan, including reducing access to medicines
Same-day contact with mental health crisis team or ED if risk can't be managed
Arrange close follow-up in days and involve a support person with consent
Start a month of sleeping tablets
Refer for psychology under a mental health treatment plan
Explain that depression is treatable and check he understands the plan
Call 000 or go to ED if he feels unsafe; give Lifeline 13 11 14 and book review in a day or two
Come back if sleep doesn't improve

extras.label: Prepare a GP mental health treatment plan today
extras.why: If time allows and it's appropriate. Safety comes first; the plan can be the next visit.

pearl: Ask about suicide directly. A safety plan, reduced access to means and close follow-up are the core of GP care.

name: Marg
who: Bookkeeper. Here for blood results.
opening: "The pharmacist said my liver tests were up?"

actions.label: Review LFTs
actions.text: GGT 240, ALT 55. Others normal.

actions.label: AUDIT-C alcohol questions
actions.text: Four glasses of wine most nights, more on weekends.
actions.why: Ask about alcohol with a validated tool, without judgement.

actions.label: Morning shakes or drinking to steady
actions.text: Sometimes a drink in the morning to settle her nerves.
actions.why: Withdrawal symptoms change how you stop safely.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Thinks it's "just the wine". Worried she's an alcoholic. Wants a liver scan.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "Since my husband died last year it's how I get to sleep."

actions.label: Abdominal and liver exam
actions.text: No signs of chronic liver disease.

actions.label: Tell her she must stop
actions.text: She goes quiet and defensive.
actions.why: Confrontation reduces change. Motivational interviewing works better.

options: Harmful alcohol use, likely dependence, with grief
Don't stop suddenly: plan supervised or medicated withdrawal
Discuss relapse prevention medicine (acamprosate or naltrexone)
Seek help if she gets shaky, sweaty, confused or has a seizure when cutting down. Review in 1 to 2 weeks

extras.label: Bill a mental health treatment plan for alcohol use alone
extras.why: Plans need a mental disorder. Alcohol use disorder can qualify, but the plan must be prepared properly.

pearl: Sudden stopping after heavy daily drinking can cause seizures. Plan withdrawal, then relapse prevention.

name: Ivan
who: Chef. Cut his hand at work.
opening: "Knife slipped. Just needs a couple of stitches."

actions.label: How and when
actions.text: Two hours ago. Clean kitchen knife.

actions.label: Tetanus status
actions.text: Last booster 12 years ago.
actions.why: Over 10 years since last dose: give a booster for a clean minor wound.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Wants to get back to work tonight.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "No, that's it."

actions.label: Check finger sensation and movement (before anaesthetic)
actions.text: Numbness on one side of the index finger tip.
actions.why: Check nerves and tendons before you numb anything.

actions.label: Test tendons individually
actions.text: Flexors intact.

actions.label: Suture it
actions.text: Done neatly.

actions.label: Refer to hand surgery
actions.text: Accepted for tomorrow's clinic.

options: Refer urgently to hand surgery for nerve repair
Clean and close the skin or dress as advised by the hand team
Suture and send back to work, no referral
Explain why the nerve matters and check he understands the plan
Come back if redness, swelling, fever or pus. Attend the hand clinic

extras.label: Bill Medicare for this work injury
extras.why: Work injuries with a workers compensation claim are billed to the insurer.

pearl: Test nerve and tendon function before local anaesthetic. A missed digital nerve injury is a lifelong loss.

name: Bree
who: Wears contact lenses.
opening: "My eye's been sore and red since yesterday. Light hurts."

actions.label: Contact lens use
actions.text: Sleeps in them sometimes. Swims with them in.
actions.why: Contact lens wear plus pain is microbial keratitis until proven otherwise.

actions.label: Visual acuity
actions.text: 6/18 in the sore eye, 6/6 in the other.
actions.why: Always check vision: reduced acuity is a red flag.

actions.label: Fluorescein stain
actions.text: A bright white-staining ulcer on the cornea.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Thinks it's conjunctivitis. Wants drops.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "No, that's it."

actions.label: Lids and discharge
actions.text: Watery. Lids normal.

actions.label: Prescribe chloramphenicol and review in a week
actions.text: Script written.
actions.why: A corneal ulcer in a lens wearer needs same-day specialist care, not just chloramphenicol.

options: Same-day ophthalmology or eye emergency referral
Stop contact lens wear and bring the lenses and case
Chloramphenicol and review in a week
Go to the eye emergency service today
Come back if it spreads to the other eye

extras.label: Bill a normal consult item
extras.why: Standard consultation.

pearl: Red flags in a red eye: pain, light sensitivity, reduced vision, contact lens wear. That's same-day specialist territory.

name: Frank
who: Lives in a residential aged care home. Nurse called.
opening: Nurse: "Frank's been agitated since yesterday and isn't himself."

actions.label: Onset and fluctuation
actions.text: Sudden, worse at night. Normally mild dementia but chatty.
actions.why: Sudden change and fluctuation point to delirium, not dementia progressing.

actions.label: Medicine review
actions.text: Oxybutynin started last week for bladder urgency.
actions.why: Anticholinergics are a common cause of delirium in older people.

actions.label: Bowels and urine
actions.text: No bowel motion for 5 days.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Family worry he's "going downhill". Nurse asks for something to calm him.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "He's not eating or drinking much."

actions.label: Observations
actions.text: Temp 37.4, pulse 96, BP 112/68.

actions.label: Abdomen
actions.text: Distended, faecal loading.

actions.label: Prescribe an antipsychotic for agitation
actions.text: Charted.
actions.why: Antipsychotics treat symptoms, add risk and don't fix causes. Use only for severe distress or danger.

options: Encourage fluids and check urine and bloods
Non-drug strategies: familiar people, glasses, hearing aids, lighting
Explain delirium to the family and nurses, and check understanding
Review in 24 to 48 hours; hospital if he gets worse, isn't drinking or has a fever

extras.label: Bill a residential aged care attendance item
extras.why: Use the aged care attendance items, not in-rooms items.

pearl: Delirium is acute, fluctuating and often has several causes. Look at medicines, constipation, urine retention, infection and dehydration.

name: Rita
who: Advanced lung cancer. Home visit. Daughter, Kim, is carer.
opening: Kim: "Mum's in a lot more pain and won't eat."

actions.label: Pain history
actions.text: Back pain, worse over a week. Taking oxycodone 10 mg twice daily.

actions.label: Leg strength and sensation
actions.text: Legs weaker. New numbness. Hasn't passed urine since morning.
actions.why: New back pain plus leg weakness in cancer is spinal cord compression until proven otherwise.

actions.label: Her goals of care
actions.text: "I want to stay home. But I don't want to be a burden."
actions.why: What she wants guides every decision.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Kim is exhausted. Worried about doing it alone.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "Is she dying?"

actions.label: Check advance care directive
actions.text: Has one. Wants comfort care but would accept treatment that helps her stay home.

actions.label: Bowels
actions.text: Constipated for 4 days.

options: Urgent discussion with palliative care and oncology about steroids and radiotherapy, in line with her wishes
Increase opioid regularly with breakthrough doses
Explain to Rita and Kim what's happening and what the options are
Call the community palliative team or you any time; review tomorrow
Call only if she stops breathing

extras.label: Bill a home visit (out-of-rooms) consult item
extras.why: Home visits use out-of-rooms items.

pearl: In cancer, new back pain plus leg weakness or bladder trouble is spinal cord compression until proven otherwise. Hours matter.

name: Barry
who: Farmer. Clinic is 3 hours from the nearest cath lab.
opening: "Had this crushing pain since I was feeding the cattle. Hour or so."

actions.label: Pain features
actions.text: Central, heavy, into the jaw. Sweaty.

actions.label: 12-lead ECG
actions.text: ST elevation in II, III and aVF.
actions.why: ECG within 10 minutes of arrival for chest pain.

actions.label: Aspirin 300 mg
actions.text: Given.

actions.label: Thrombolysis contraindications checklist
actions.text: None. No recent bleeding, surgery or stroke.
actions.why: If PCI can't happen within about 2 hours, thrombolysis is usually indicated.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Wants to know if he can drive home to tell his wife.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "I've had a bit of indigestion all week."

actions.label: Observations
actions.text: BP 128/80, pulse 58, sats 97%.

actions.label: Call retrieval and cardiology hotline
actions.text: Retrieval coordinated; telehealth cardiologist advises thrombolysis.

options: Thrombolysis (after cardiology advice and consent), then transfer for angiography
Aspirin and anticoagulation as per protocol
Organise retrieval to a PCI hospital
Wait to see if pain settles
Explain the heart attack and treatment, and check he understands
Staying with him until retrieval arrives; continuous monitoring and defibrillator ready
Drive to hospital in the morning

extras.label: Bill an after-hours or emergency attendance item if eligible
extras.why: Rural generalists often provide emergency care; check the specific item rules.

pearl: In rural STEMI, time is muscle. If PCI isn't possible within 2 hours of first contact, thrombolysis plus transfer is usual.

name: Amina
who: Arrived from Afghanistan 4 months ago. Speaks Dari.
opening: Her husband: "She has headaches. I translate."

actions.label: Book a phone interpreter (TIS)
actions.text: A female Dari interpreter joins. Amina speaks more freely.
actions.why: Family members shouldn't interpret, especially for women's health or sensitive topics.

actions.label: Headache story
actions.text: Daily tension-type headaches. No red flags.

actions.label: Sleep and mood
actions.text: Nightmares about the journey. Startles easily.
actions.why: Trauma symptoms are common and often present as physical complaints.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: She worries she has a brain tumour. Wants painkillers.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "I'm also worried about my periods. And my children haven't had their needles."

actions.label: Neuro exam and fundi
actions.text: Normal.

actions.label: Refugee health screening bloods
actions.text: Ordered: FBC, iron, vitamin D, hep B and C, HIV, syphilis, strongyloides, IGRA, schistosoma.

options: Tension headaches with likely trauma-related symptoms (PTSD)
Use a professional interpreter at every visit
Arrange post-arrival health screening and catch-up vaccines for the whole family
Refer to a torture and trauma counselling service
Come back if headaches change, wake her, or with weakness or vomiting. Review in 2 weeks with an interpreter

extras.label: Bill the patient for the interpreter
extras.why: TIS National provides free interpreting for GP consults that are Medicare-rebatable.

pearl: Use a professional interpreter. Family interpreting misses trauma, women's health and safety issues.

name: Chloe
who: Two young kids. Partner waits in the car.
opening: "I tripped over the kids' toys. It's fine, just sore."

actions.label: Make sure she's seen alone
actions.text: Her partner's outside; she seems more relaxed.
actions.why: Ask about violence only when it's safe and private.

actions.label: Ask directly about safety at home
actions.text: Pause. "He gets angry. He grabbed me."
actions.why: Asking directly, kindly, is how disclosure happens.

actions.label: Risk assessment: strangulation, threats, weapons, escalation
actions.text: He choked her once last month.
actions.why: Non-fatal strangulation is a strong predictor of later homicide.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Scared that if she tells, the kids will be taken.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "Don't write anything down. He reads my phone."

actions.label: Wrist exam
actions.text: Finger-pattern bruising. Bones fine.

actions.label: Suggest couples counselling
actions.text: She looks worried.
actions.why: Couples counselling isn't safe in family violence.

options: Intimate partner violence with high-risk features
Safety plan, including a safe way to contact her
Connect with specialist family violence services (1800RESPECT)
Document carefully in the record, with privacy settings
Agree a safe way to follow up; 000 if in danger

extras.label: Send an SMS appointment reminder
extras.why: Her partner reads her phone. Ask about safe contact methods first.

pearl: Ask about strangulation. It's one of the strongest warning signs of future lethal violence.

name: Jake
who: Uni student. Partner just tested positive.
opening: "Got a text from a contact tracing service. A guy I hooked up with has gonorrhoea."

actions.label: Sexual history (partners, practices, protection)
actions.text: Two male partners in 3 months. Receptive anal and oral sex. Condoms sometimes.
actions.why: Sites tested depend on practices.

actions.label: Symptoms
actions.text: None.

actions.label: PrEP
actions.text: Not on PrEP. Hasn't heard much about it.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Embarrassed. Wants to "get it sorted today".

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "Do I need to tell the other guy?"

actions.label: Test throat, rectal swab and urine, plus HIV, syphilis, hep B serology
actions.text: Done.

actions.label: Urine test only
actions.text: Done.
actions.why: Urine alone misses throat and rectal infections.

options: Gonorrhoea contact: test all sites and treat as contact
Treat as a contact today (ceftriaxone IM + azithromycin as per guideline)
Test all exposed sites and blood tests
Offer PrEP and hep A and B vaccination
Test of cure as advised; no sex for 7 days after treatment and until partners treated

extras.label: Bill a normal consult item
extras.why: Sexual health consults are standard Medicare items.

pearl: Test sites according to practices. Treat contacts on the day. Every STI visit is a chance to offer PrEP and vaccines.

name: Zoe
who: Year 10. Mum brought her in, then waits outside.
opening: "Mum made me come. My stomach hurts before school."

actions.label: Explain confidentiality and its limits
actions.text: "So you won't tell Mum?" She relaxes a bit.
actions.why: Young people open up when they know what stays private and the safety exceptions.

actions.label: HEEADSSS psychosocial assessment
actions.text: Being bullied online. Skipping lunch to avoid people. Sleeping badly.
actions.why: Somatic symptoms in teens often have psychosocial drivers.

actions.label: Self-harm and safety
actions.text: Some thoughts of not wanting to be here, no plan.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Wants the tummy aches to stop. Scared Mum will find out about the bullying.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "Can I come back by myself?"

actions.label: Abdominal exam
actions.text: Normal.

actions.label: Refer for a gastroscopy
actions.text: Ordered.
actions.why: A normal exam and no red flags don't need scoping.

options: Functional abdominal pain with anxiety, low mood and bullying
Link to youth mental health support (headspace)
With her consent, involve Mum or school
Come back by herself in a week; Kids Helpline 1800 55 1800 any time

extras.label: She can have her own Medicare card from 14
extras.why: Young people 14 and over can get their own Medicare card.

pearl: See young people on their own for part of the consult. Explain confidentiality first.

name: Lou
who: Type 2 diabetes for 20 years.
opening: "Got a blister on my foot. Doesn't hurt much."

actions.label: How long
actions.text: Three weeks. Didn't notice till he saw blood on his sock.

actions.label: Foot exam: pulses, monofilament, ulcer probe
actions.text: No pedal pulses. Can't feel monofilament. Ulcer probes to bone.
actions.why: Probe-to-bone suggests osteomyelitis.

actions.label: Signs of infection
actions.text: Redness spreading 3 cm. Warm.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Worried about "losing the foot". Wants a cream.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "My sugars have been high."

actions.label: Antiseptic cream and review in 2 weeks
actions.text: Prescribed.
actions.why: Infected deep diabetic ulcers with poor circulation need urgent specialist care.

options: Infected diabetic foot ulcer with likely osteomyelitis and ischaemia
Same-day referral to the high-risk foot service or hospital
Start antibiotics as per guideline after cultures
Explain why it's urgent and check he understands
Today: high-risk foot service or ED

extras.label: Refer to podiatry with a chronic disease management plan
extras.why: Allied health items need a GP chronic condition management plan.

pearl: Diabetes plus foot ulcer with infection or ischaemia is a limb emergency.

name: Nick
who: Stonemason for 15 years.
opening: "Getting puffed carrying slabs. Mate said I should get checked."

actions.label: Occupational history: dust, masks, ventilation
actions.text: Cut engineered stone dry for years, often without a mask.
actions.why: Ask "What do you do, and what are you exposed to?"

actions.label: Smoking
actions.text: Never.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Worried about his job and his family's income.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "A few blokes I worked with have the same."

actions.label: Chest exam
actions.text: Fine crackles at the bases.

actions.label: Spirometry
actions.text: Restrictive pattern.

actions.label: Chest CT (HRCT)
actions.text: Small nodules in upper lobes.

options: Notify under state dust disease scheme and workers compensation
Explain silicosis, what it means for work, and check understanding
Come back if more breathless or coughing blood; respiratory review booked

extras.label: Bill Medicare for the workers compensation consult
extras.why: If it becomes a claim, consults are billed to the insurer.

pearl: Always take an occupational history. Engineered stone was banned in Australia from July 2024 because of silicosis.

name: Vince
who: Accountant.
opening: "Bit awkward. Things aren't working downstairs. Can I get the blue pills?"

actions.label: Erectile history
actions.text: Gradual over a year. No morning erections.

actions.label: Cardiovascular risk factors
actions.text: Smokes. Father had a heart attack at 60. Never had cholesterol checked.
actions.why: Erectile dysfunction is an early marker of cardiovascular disease.

actions.label: Nitrates or chest pain
actions.text: No nitrates. Sometimes chest tightness on hills.
actions.why: PDE5 inhibitors with nitrates can drop BP dangerously.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Embarrassed. Wants a quick script.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "My wife thinks I'm stressed."

actions.label: Lipids, HbA1c, morning testosterone
actions.text: Ordered.

options: ED as a marker of vascular disease, with possible angina
Assess cardiovascular risk and investigate the exertional chest tightness
Discuss PDE5 inhibitor once cardiac status is clear
Script for sildenafil today without further checks
Come back with results in 1 to 2 weeks; ambulance if chest pain at rest or lasting over 10 minutes
Only if the pills don't work

extras.label: Bill a heart health check
extras.why: If he meets the criteria and it's done properly, a heart health assessment item may apply.

pearl: Erectile dysfunction often appears years before heart disease. Treat it as a vascular warning sign.

name: Ruth
who: Phone telehealth. You saw her 3 months ago.
opening: "Can you just do my repeats over the phone, love?"

actions.label: Confirm identity and location
actions.text: Name, DOB confirmed. She's at home.
actions.why: Confirm identity and where they are in case of emergency.

actions.label: Medicine review
actions.text: On warfarin, ramipril, metformin. Bruising more easily.

actions.label: Check INR record
actions.text: Last INR 4.1 two weeks ago, no follow-up recorded.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Hates driving to the clinic. Wants e-scripts sent.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "I had a little fall last week, nothing much."

actions.label: Ask about the fall
actions.text: Hit her head. Mild headache since.
actions.why: Head injury on warfarin needs a CT.

actions.label: Send e-scripts
actions.text: Sent.

options: Head injury on warfarin with a high INR
Repeat scripts and review in 3 months
Explain why she needs a scan today, and check she understands
Go to ED today; call 000 if drowsy, vomiting or confused

extras.label: Bill a phone telehealth item
extras.why: She's an established patient (seen in the last 12 months), so the telehealth items apply.

pearl: Telehealth still needs a proper history. "Anything else?" can reveal the emergency.

name: Pam
who: Retired nurse.
opening: "Woke up and the room was spinning. Vomited twice."

actions.label: Onset and triggers
actions.text: Constant since waking, not just with head movement.
actions.why: Continuous vertigo is different from brief positional vertigo.

actions.label: Other neuro symptoms
actions.text: Some trouble walking. No speech change.

actions.label: HINTS exam (head impulse, nystagmus, test of skew)
actions.text: Normal head impulse. Direction-changing nystagmus.
actions.why: Normal head impulse plus direction-changing nystagmus suggests a central (stroke) cause.

actions.label: Gait
actions.text: Can't walk without help.

actions.label: Ideas, concerns, expectations
actions.text: Thinks it's "an inner ear thing". Wants tablets for nausea.

actions.label: "Anything else?"
actions.text: "I've got high blood pressure and AF."

actions.label: Epley manoeuvre
actions.text: Makes it worse.
actions.why: Epley is for BPPV, not continuous vertigo.

options: Ambulance to ED for stroke assessment
Come back if it lasts a week

extras.label: Bill a normal consult item
extras.why: Standard consultation.

pearl: Continuous vertigo plus can't walk, or HINTS pointing central, needs stroke assessment.
